hypotheses.justification: Replace the proof's use of exists_algebra_finiteType fX by exists_algebra_finiteType (h ≫ fY). IsFinite h supplies LocallyOfFiniteType h, and locallyOfFiniteType_comp supplies LocallyOfFiniteType (h ≫ fY). Everything else is unchanged; no compatibility between fX, fY and h is required. The point x ensures the affine neighborhoods used are nonempty. Each finite-type hypothesis is independently deletable, but in general they cannot both be dropped.

Retain the affine reduction, writing B → A for its integral injection and P over Q for the selected primes. Only A needs to be finite type over K. Every prime P' over Q has the same height as P: the integral injections B/Q → A/P' and B/Q → A/P give equal quotient dimensions by ringKrullDim_eq_of_isIntegral_of_injective, and Ideal.height_add_ringKrullDim_quotient_eq_ringKrullDim_of_finiteType applied in A gives equal heights. Lift any finite prime chain ending at Q using exists_ltSeries_comap_eq_last; its lift ends at such a P', so height Q ≤ height P. Conversely, contraction preserves strict prime chains under an integral map, as in the existing ringKrullDim_eq_of_isIntegral_of_injective proof. Thus the heights agree without finite type for B. All dimensions used in cancellation are finite because A and its prime quotients are finite-type domains over K; x excludes empty neighborhoods. The other finite-type hypothesis is retained; in general both cannot be dropped.

On the chosen affine neighborhoods, let φ : B → A and I = ker φ. Surjectivity of h implies every prime of B contains I. Replace B by B/I: it is a domain since RingHom.kerLift_injective embeds it into the domain A, remains finite type over K, and its map to A is integral by RingHom.IsIntegral.kerLift. Apply the existing height_comap_eq to this injection. Ideal.primeSpectrumQuotientOrderIsoZeroLocus identifies Spec(B/I) with all of Spec(B), since every prime contains I, so the corresponding prime heights are unchanged. The existing stalk-localization argument finishes. This explicitly handles nonreduced targets; x makes the neighborhoods and quotient domain nontrivial.
